
Two arXiv papers from the RSS feed meet ≥3 inclusion criteria with strong signal: AnovaX addresses multi-agent orchestration with typed executors and adaptive recovery; the Behavioral Controllability paper directly examines the architectural spectrum from fixed workflows to reflective agents.

## Suggestions

- [AnovaX: A Local, Multi-Agent Voice Assistant with LLM Planning, Typed Executors, and Adaptive Recovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15367) — Presents a multi-agent architecture with LLM-based planning, typed executor design, and adaptive recovery mechanisms, grounding agentic workflow patterns in a production-style local deployment.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (multi-agent orchestration, typed executors), Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (LLM planning, typed execution), Iterative refinement practices (adaptive recovery loops), Empirical or practical grounding (production-style local deployment)

- [Behavioral Controllability of Agentic Models for Information Extraction: From Fixed Workflows to Reflective Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15715) — Examines the architectural spectrum from fixed agentic workflows to reflective agents for information extraction, providing principled analysis of controllability, workflow design patterns, and iterative self-correction.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (fixed vs. reflective workflow architectures), Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (workflow execution patterns), Iterative refinement practices (reflective agent self-correction loops)
